title: CIDR Subnet Calculator
h1: CIDR Subnet Calculator — IPv4 Network, Hosts and Mask
seoTitle: CIDR Subnet Calculator — IPv4 Mask, Range and Hosts
description: Calculate the IPv4 network address, broadcast, usable host range, subnet mask, and host count from an IP and CIDR prefix. Computed locally, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Enter an IPv4 address and a prefix length from 0 to 32. The calculator shows the network, broadcast, usable range, subnet mask, wildcard mask, and host count.
blurb: Find the IPv4 network, broadcast, usable hosts, and subnet mask for any CIDR prefix.

controls.label: Prefix length
controls.help: The number after the slash in CIDR notation, such as /24.

howItWorks: Enter any IPv4 address and the CIDR prefix length from 0 to 32.
Press Calculate subnet to mask the address and derive the network and broadcast.
Read the usable host range, subnet mask, wildcard mask, and total host count.
examples: A /32 is a single host address with no separate network and broadcast split.

faq.q: Which IP version does this support?
faq.a: IPv4 only. Each octet must be an integer from 0 to 255, and the prefix must be an integer from 0 to 32.

faq.q: Why can the usable host count be zero?
faq.a: For /31 and /32 there is no traditional network-plus-broadcast pair with spare hosts. /31 is often used as a point-to-point link, and /32 is a single address.

faq.q: Is the address looked up online?
faq.a: No. The mask math runs in your browser. The tool does not check who owns the address.
